hero: On a medicine ward of a provincial hospital in Batangas, a Filipino resident gently palpates the right lower abdomen of a middle-aged Filipino woman with a kidney transplant, while her husband holds a plastic bag of medicine boxes and a nurse checks an IV line; late evening fluorescent light, calm concentration, no text.

figures.teaches: The likely causes of allograft dysfunction depend on time since transplant.
figures.content: Horizontal timeline with three colored bands. Band 1 'First week': delayed graft function, renal artery or vein thrombosis, urine leak, obstruction, hyperacute or early antibody-mediated rejection. Band 2 '1-6 months': acute T-cell- or antibody-mediated rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, BK nephropathy, obstruction or lymphocele, pyelonephritis, volume depletion, CMV. Band 3 'After 6 months': antibody-mediated rejection (donor-specific antibodies, missed doses), drug toxicity, recurrent glomerular disease, transplant renal artery stenosis, chronic injury. Beneath: work-up strip 'Repeat creatinine - volume and drugs - trough level - Doppler ultrasound - urine protein, plasma BK DNA, DSA - biopsy (KDIGO 2009 R7.1, 1C)'.

figures.teaches: Common drugs and conditions raise or lower tacrolimus levels through the same metabolic pathway.
figures.content: Central vertical gauge labeled 'Tacrolimus level' with a target band in the middle. Upward red arrow 'Raises level: toxicity, rising creatinine, high potassium' listing clarithromycin, erythromycin, azole antifungals, diltiazem, verapamil, grapefruit, diarrhea. Downward blue arrow 'Lowers level: rejection' listing rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St John's wort, missed doses, vomiting. Side box 'Brand switch: level may move either way - check a trough'. Footer 'KDIGO 2009: monitor levels with rifampin (1C); check levels after medication change (2C)'.

card: A pill organizer with several tacrolimus boxes of different brands beside a laboratory request slip on a table, no text.
